title: Getting Started with sigRecon
text: Given gene signature XX describing genetic chemical perturbation one biological context (cell line, tissue), corresponding gene signature perturbation different context? method takes ranked list genes source context outputs ranked list genes target context performing signature recontextualization. sigrecon provides three baseline recontextualization methods – projection-based scoring (projectCor()), network propagation (netProp()), DESeq2-based mean method (recontextualize(method = "mean")) – plus benchmarking tools (sig_eval_table()) evaluate well recontextualized signature recovers true signature target context. vignette walks three methods end end small, bundled real-data example, requiring downloads external setup.

title: Getting Started with sigRecon
text: mean method takes different approach entirely: rather recontextualizing signature already , derives one directly target-context expression data, running DESeq2 perturbed control samples keeping top upregulated genes. needs raw counts sample metadata identifying samples perturbed vs. control (), doesn’t fit SciPlex demo signatures used – ’s minimal, fabricated example showing shape inputs: g1/g2 two genes consistently higher pertA samples controls, come derived signature pertA.
code: set.seed(42) n_genes <- 30  # g1/g2 are upregulated 4x in pertA samples; everything else is unperturbed noise. ctrl_base <- rnbinom(n_genes, mu = 200, size = 10) pert_base <- ctrl_base pert_base[1:2] <- pert_base[1:2] * 4  sample_counts <- function(base, n) {   sapply(seq_len(n), function(i) rnbinom(length(base), mu = pmax(base, 1), size = 10)) }  counts <- cbind(sample_counts(ctrl_base, 4), sample_counts(pert_base, 3)) rownames(counts) <- paste0("g", seq_len(n_genes)) colnames(counts) <- c(paste0("ctrl", 1:4), paste0("pertA", 1:3))  coldata <- S4Vectors::DataFrame(   perturbation = c(rep("control", 4), rep("pertA", 3)),   condition    = c(rep("Control", 4), rep("Perturbed", 3)),   row.names    = colnames(counts) )  se_mean <- SummarizedExperiment(assays = list(counts = counts), colData = coldata)  recon_mean <- recontextualize(   method = "mean",   se = se_mean,   perturbation_col = "perturbation",   condition_col = "condition",   alpha = 1,   limit = 2 ) recon_mean #> $pertA #> [1] "g2" "g1"

what: avg_p: ensembling over a range of restart values
title: Network Propagation in Depth
text: Picking single “right” p given network always obvious. Setting avg_p = TRUE instead runs random walk avg_p_length restart values evenly spaced across avg_p_vals range averages resulting stationary probabilities – trading single, possibly-arbitrary choice p smoother estimate less sensitive choice.
code: sig_avg_p <- network_sig(   network,   seeds = one_seed,   sig = "rwr",   avg_p = TRUE,   avg_p_vals = c(0.05, 0.5),   avg_p_length = 5,   limit = 30 ) #> Using weighted graph #> Reached Convergence. Iteration step: 26 #> Reached Convergence. Iteration step: 20 #> Reached Convergence. Iteration step: 16 #> Reached Convergence. Iteration step: 13 #> Reached Convergence. Iteration step: 10 length(sig_avg_p[[1]]) #> [1] 30

what: bootstrap/n_bootstraps: significance-based selection instead of top-limit
title: Network Propagation in Depth
text: default (bootstrap = FALSE), network_sig() just keeps top limit genes stationary probability – arbitrary cutoff. Setting bootstrap = TRUE instead runs random walk n_bootstraps randomly-chosen gene sets (matched size real seed set) build empirical null distribution, keeps genes whose real stationary probability exceeds 99th percentile null – significance-based cutoff rather fixed count. means resulting signature can smaller (larger) limit, costs roughly n_bootstraps extra random walks per seed set, ’s noticeably slower.
code: sig_bootstrap <- network_sig(   network,   seeds = one_seed,   sig = "rwr",   bootstrap = TRUE,   n_bootstraps = 30, # kept small here for vignette speed; real analyses may want more   limit = 30 # unused when bootstrap = TRUE and p != 1, but harmless to leave set ) #> Using weighted graph #> Reached Convergence. Iteration step: 23 #> Reached Convergence. Iteration step: 56 length(sig_bootstrap[[1]]) #> [1] 24
